title: Buttery swede and leeks with fried eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain staple: butter, swede, leeks, tinned butter beans, eggs, watercress, lemon and thyme.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday Tesco purchase at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only two frying pans, one with a lid, a bowl and simple steam-frying and egg-frying.

works.reason: Diced swede steamed for 10 minutes in butter and water will be tender, then crisps with the leeks, and a small swede with a tin of beans and two eggs each is enough for four.

honest_times.reason: 20 minutes covers peeling and dicing a small swede, slicing leeks and the active frying, and the 10 unattended minutes match the covered cook, so it stays quick.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including thyme and lemon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Swede is the bulk of a warm buttery pan supper, which suits late October.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Root veg, leeks, beans, eggs and greens make a filling, balanced dinner a family would happily eat again.
